headline: High: caveman’s MCP-enabled content-writing workflow can feed social-auto-upload’s broad-network uploader, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md and memory files, while social-auto-upload operates on uploaded media and account data. A shared file or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content from caveman influence upload instructions, though direct default ingestion is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange prompts or captions through a shared file or MCP channel, injection becomes plausible.
IF social-auto-upload parses caveman-authored text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable any shared prompt/file bridge between the agents.
Require a human review step for captions, prompts, and metadata.
Store caveman outputs in a read-only staging folder.
Use allowlisted templates for upload instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening for any shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while social-auto-upload touches account data and has broad network egress. If either agent is pointed at a shared workspace, sensitive notes or account artifacts could flow into the uploader’s outbound requests. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-style workflows, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or account files, leakage risk increases.
IF social-auto-upload sends locally stored captions, images, or account metadata to remote services, those contents may leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for notes and upload assets.
Keep session logs and memory files out of the uploader’s directory.
Review outbound requests before upload runs.
Use a dedicated low-sensitivity account for testing.
requires-engineering: enforce filesystem and network egress boundaries per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances, but social-auto-upload cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or execute shell commands. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only or external API use. Because the pair lacks shared mutable write surfaces in the profiles, conflict stays low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk rises.
IF a shared account file is mutated outside the uploader’s built-in scope, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize any manual edits to shared files.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same account artifact.
Use file locks for any shared state.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman produces content-writing outputs and social-auto-upload is a publishing tool that can act on those outputs. If upload captions or metadata are taken from caveman without verification, a bad draft can cascade into a public post. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, but the pathway is credible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes caveman-generated captions or descriptions without review, errors can propagate to published content.
IF caveman is used to draft account-facing text, downstream publication may amplify mistakes.
mitigations: Add a human approval step before publishing.
Compare generated text against a checklist before upload.
Use a dry-run mode for new workflows.
Limit caveman output to drafts, not final posts.
requires-engineering: implement validation rules for publishable metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman handles session logs, memory files, and project notes, while social-auto-upload handles account data and broad network egress. If those data classes include regulated or personal content, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches when notes are pushed into an uploader that transmits externally. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF project notes or session logs contain personal data and are reused in upload metadata, compliance obligations may attach.
IF account data is processed in a jurisdiction with stricter retention rules than the uploader’s defaults, mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Avoid placing personal data in project notes.
Redact account identifiers before upload.
Set a short manual retention window for logs.
Document the data flow for each posting workflow.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both agents.
